title: kbmon --events: ops rows, coord events and delivery outcomes as event and span records with id-only attributes
goal: python3 _tools/kbmon.py --events [--since CURSOR] prints one JSON object with a cursor, the events (coord events, done.refused rows and query-log delivery outcomes) and the spans (each landing with a child span per land.step, each agent.run, each test.run and each delivery whose time the log gives) newer than the cursor, each with times in Unix nanoseconds and attributes that are numbers, flags or ids that passed redact.redact; a second call with the returned cursor repeats none of them

clauses.clause: python3 _tools/kbmon.py --events [--since CURSOR] prints one JSON object with a cursor, the events (coord events, done.refused rows and query-log delivery outcomes) and the spans (each landing with a child span per land.step, each agent.run, each test.run and each delivery whose time the log gives) newer than the cursor, each with times in Unix nanoseconds and attributes that are numbers, flags or ids that passed redact.redact
a second call with the returned cursor repeats none of them

gates.question: What does the --events cursor hold?
options: the newest spool row time and coord sequence, as one opaque text
gates.recommendation: the newest spool row time and coord sequence, as one opaque text
gates.answer: the newest spool row time and coord sequence, as one opaque text

gates.question: What is a delivery span, since the log gives one time for it?
options: start equal to end at the log's last write, only when the log gives that time
gates.recommendation: start equal to end at the log's last write, only when the log gives that time
gates.answer: start equal to end at the log's last write, only when the log gives that time

gates.question: When is a landing exported as a span?
options: once its land.end row is in the log, with the steps of its item in its span
as soon as a land.step row is seen, with an open end
gates.recommendation: once its land.end row is in the log, with the steps of its item in its span
gates.answer: once its land.end row is in the log, with the steps of its item in its span

gates.question: How does an attribute hold a list of ids, and what happens to an attribute that is no number, flag or stable id?
options: the attribute is left out and the record stays; a list is name_n (its length) and name_1.. (the first four)
the whole record is left out, as a metric point is; a list is one attribute joined by a comma
gates.recommendation: the attribute is left out and the record stays; a list is name_n (its length) and name_1.. (the first four)
gates.answer: the attribute is left out and the record stays; a list is name_n (its length) and name_1.. (the first four)

gates.question: How much does a call without --since return?
options: the newest 4000 ops rows' records and the newest 1000 coord events
gates.recommendation: the newest 4000 ops rows' records and the newest 1000 coord events
gates.answer: the newest 4000 ops rows' records and the newest 1000 coord events

gates.question: What are a span's id and trace?
options: 16 hex characters of a hash of the ops row's id, and the landing root's id as the trace of its steps
the ops row's own id, one trace id for all
gates.recommendation: 16 hex characters of a hash of the ops row's id, and the landing root's id as the trace of its steps
gates.answer: 16 hex characters of a hash of the ops row's id, and the landing root's id as the trace of its steps

notes: Plan 2026-10-18: kbmon stays read-only, so the cursor is the caller's to keep. coord event fields are ids by coord.py's own rule, and id-shaped fake secrets (IDS in the check) pass it, so the redaction is proved on them. Plan 2026-10-18: reuses mon_log.py's reader of coord events and ops rows; the cursor and the span records are this item's. check 0 plants a random item id per run: the fixed ST-dddddddd collided with a worker's sample rows delivered into the committed query log on 2026-10-18, so done saw two landing spans
